title: +PSYCHOLOGY OF RACE AND RACISM
description: Introduces psychological theories and concepts pertaining to different racial groups in the United States. Explores historical and contemporary racism in the U.S. and its psychological effect on racial identity and the intersections of race, ethnicity, sex, gender identity, social class, and nationality. Explores racism and intersecting forms of oppression in the discipline of psychology. Develops cultural competence and humility to prepare students to live and work with individuals from diverse socio-cultural backgrounds.
registration_restrictions:
Prerequisites: (PSY 201, 201H, 201Z or 201HZ) and (PSY 202, 202H, 202Z or 202HZ).
A minimum grade of C- is required in PSY 201, PSY 201H, PSY 201Z, PSY 201HZ, PSY 202, PSY 202H, PSY 202Z and PSY 202HZ.

Students with a term class standing of Freshman or Sophomore may not enroll.
recommendations: Completion of a Difference, Power, and Oppression Foundations course
attribute_description: Core Education - Difference, Power, & Oppression: Advanced (CSDP)
books_html: No-cost: Course utilizes open educational resources, materials available through the library, or does not require any purchased materials.
